questions.stem: What is due diligence, in general terms?
options: A contract signed after a merger completes
An enquiry, inspection or assessment carried out to check the evidence or specifics of a matter under attention
A report produced by the finance team each quarter
A technique for anonymising data before sharing
The process of migrating data to the cloud
questions.explanation: Due diligence is the investigation or exercise of care a reasonable business or person takes to check the facts before entering into an agreement or act.

questions.stem: Which everyday example illustrates due diligence when buying something?
options: Paying by credit card rather than cash
Asking a friend for the Wi-Fi password
Checking which country it was made in, whether it is new or used, which company produced it and its quality
questions.explanation: Checks such as country of origin, condition, manufacturer and quality before buying are all part of a due diligence process.

questions.stem: In which long-established business process is due diligence described as a must?
questions.explanation: The merger and acquisition process is a very old process in which due diligence is a must before buying or merging with a company.

options: Validating imported data against its source
A check conducted by the acquiring or both parties in a merger or acquisition to make sure the deal is profitable in terms of data
Running distinct counts on every column of a dataset
Encrypting confidential data before a company is sold
Cataloguing all tables and columns in a database
questions.explanation: Because data has become one of the most valuable assets, the parties to a merger or acquisition conduct Data Due Diligence to ensure the deal is in profit in terms of data.

questions.stem: When buying a data-oriented company such as Uber, Amazon or Facebook, what will the buyer chiefly evaluate?
questions.explanation: For a data-oriented company the buyer evaluates data assets rather than physical assets.

questions.stem: For which roles is a Data Due Diligence report described as key for decision making?
questions.explanation: A report based on Data Due Diligence is a key input for the CDO, CFO and CEO in decision making.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed among the Data Due Diligence processes?
questions.explanation: Valuation, synergies, liabilities and ownerships are all on the list; Data Vectorisation is a processing technique, not a due diligence process.

questions.stem: Which of these appears in the list of Data Due Diligence processes?
questions.explanation: Data Lineage Availability is among the processes, alongside Data Health or Quality, Data Governance Practices and Data Security and Privacy Practices.

questions.stem: Why has Data Due Diligence become relevant to mergers and acquisitions in the recent era?
options: Because regulators now require it for every purchase
Because physical assets no longer have value
Because cloud storage has become cheap
Because data has become one of the most valuable assets of an organisation
questions.explanation: As data has become one of an organisation's most valuable assets, deals must be evaluated in terms of data as well as other assets.

questions.stem: Which pair of items both appear among the Data Due Diligence processes?
questions.explanation: Data Risk and Data Challenges are both listed, together with Data Opportunities, Data Assets and Analytical Capabilities.
